newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields lower on foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields lower on foreign markets.

text.p: Swedish debt yields fell slightly on Wednesday morning on stronger foreign markets while the crown firmed marginally on foreign interest.
"We are chiefly influenced by German interest rates, which first followed the U.S. market and then the German bund passed a resistance level," one dealer said.
Ten year bond yields fell three basis points to 6.59 percent while the six month T-bill rate was unchanged at 4.12 percent.
The difference between Swedish and German ten-year debt yields increased by three basis points to 94 basis points.
Dealers said this was partly due to an 1050 GMT auction of the Swedish 10-year bond. "After the auction I think the spread could start decreasing," one dealer said.
Dealers said there had been increasing interest in technical levels for the 10-year bond but opinions were divided on exact resistance levels.
One dealer said the resistance level was broken at 6.60 percent and the next level was 6.55 percent but another dealer saw a resistance level at 6.57 percent.
The crown was trading at 4.4350 to the mark vs 4.4400 late Tuesday. -- Olof Swahnberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1019
